report:
Phase 8 held-out round 2, files processes.md and binaries.md. Result: 20 failures, all instances of known classes, no new class, no new MUST.

Method
- I extracted 56 runnable cells with a script: the 14 pipeline blocks P1..P14, the inline rg cells of CS-PROC-01..25, G1, and the rg cells of CS-BIN-02..26. I ran each verbatim, with SRC=src, on all 5 trees (280 runs).
- Three cells need files no tree has, so I ran them on synthetic fixtures. The pin jq gate was green on the genuine file and exited 1 on a 63-character pin and an empty `pins`. A trailing-newline pin also exited 1 (my first fixture was malformed; the second one verified it). eng/triangulate.py behaved as stated: it exits 1 on a version with no manifest row and on an altered checksum line. The canary dotnet block needs a canary project nobody has, so it is not counted as a run.
- I also re-ran all 56 cells retargeted to the real shape (`SRC=src/Bicep.RpcClient`, `src/Bootstrap` mapped to the installer directory).
- Independent second greps covered Process and Kill use, StreamWriter and encoding, HttpClient shapes, hash use, certificate callbacks, archive extraction and architecture detection.
- I compiled two probes (netstandard2.0 and net8.0/net10.0) in /home/mherwig/.cache/research-lang/dotnet-tools/fixtures/heldout2-procbin/.
- The held-out clones are untouched; `git status` is clean on all five. No mktemp was used and nothing was left in the shared heldout2-tmp directory.

Trees and applicability
- Only Azure/bicep launches processes and downloads a binary. It has five launch seams: DockerCredentialProvider, BicepClient, BicepInstaller (a `chmod` shell-out), GrpcLocalExtension and the VS ClientProcessLauncher.
- Bicep.RpcClient is the closest match to the reference shape. It is a library that wraps and downloads the Bicep CLI, but it deliberately targets netstandard2.0.
- refit (HTTP client library, source generators), UniTask (Unity), NSubstitute and GuardClauses launch nothing and download nothing. Every PROC/BIN cell is tag-silent there. Hits on refit and UniTask are therefore out-of-scope noise, not defects.
- Hits per cell, listed as refit/UniTask/NSubstitute/bicep/GuardClauses:
  - Empty on all 5: P1, P4, P5, P7, P13, PROC-02#2, 06, 11, 14#1, 14#3, 15#1, 17, 18, 19#1, 19#2, 25#1-4, G1, and BIN-02, 05, 06, 07, 10, 16, 22, 24, 25, 26.
  - P2: 0/0/0/11/0. P3: 0/0/0/12/0. P6: 0/0/0/1/0. P8: 3/0/0/0/0. P10: 3/0/0/6/0.
  - P9: prints `MISSING one seam file` on all 5 (bicep has 5 seams, the others 0).
  - CS-PROC-01#1: 0/0/0/3/0, so the other four print empty and the wiring cell fails there by design.
  - CS-PROC-02#1: 0/0/0/5/0. CS-PROC-03#1: 0/0/0/6/0. CS-PROC-07#1: 0/0/0/2/0. CS-PROC-14#2: 0/0/0/10/0.
  - CS-PROC-15#2: 1/1/0/0/0.
  - BIN-08: 0/1/0/28/0. BIN-14: 80/0/0/5/0. BIN-15#2: 2/0/0/0/0. BIN-17: 0/0/0/2/0.
  - BIN-11#1: 82/0/0/3/0. BIN-11#2: 35/2/0/8/0.
  - P11, P14 and CS-PROC-19#3 hard-code `src/Process`; BIN-12 and BIN-13 hard-code `src/Bootstrap`. All exit 2 on every tree. That is documented as "rename" and is read as a failure, not a pass.
- Hit judgments, up to 10 per cell:
  - P2: 1 true positive (`BicepDeploymentStartParams(... string token ...)` is a real bearer token with no PrintMembers) and 10 false positives (JToken, SemanticToken, TokenType).
  - P3: 11 true positives. The chmod `RedirectStandardOutput` that is never decoded is benign.
  - P6: the single hit is an unused `using System.Security.AccessControl`.
  - P10: 9 of 9 false positives (UnmatchedTokens, JTokenExpression, tokensSent, secretVersion).
  - CS-PROC-03: 1 true positive (`FileName = "chmod"`) and 5 false positives (`const string FileName = "main.json"`).
  - CS-PROC-14#2: 10 true positives, all the VS Job Object (see failure 5).
  - BIN-08: 3 true positives of 28 (the RpcClient `VersionRegex`, the OCI `^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$` and the docker-helper-name regex). The other 25 are compiler and linter regexes.
  - BIN-11#1: 3 of 3 true positives. BIN-11#2: 2 true positives (BicepInstaller lines 56 and 74) and 6 false positives (Azure SDK `.GetAsync`).
  - BIN-14: 1 true positive (`new HttpClient()` in McpServer), 1 AddHttpClient registration, 3 `CreateClient()` method false positives.
  - BIN-17: 1 true positive (`"chmod"`) and 1 false positive (the text "ExecutionPolicy" in a linter message).
- Retargeted to Bicep.RpcClient, the cells fire on real defects: chmod, BIN-11 (`GetAsync` without `ResponseHeadersRead`, `ReadAsStringAsync`), the unanchored `$` version regex, bare `CreateDirectory`, and `FileName="chmod"`.

Claims re-verified (faithful, not failures)
- CS-PROC-16: net8.0 and net10.0 throw ArgumentOutOfRange at -2 ms and at 50 days, accept 49 days, and cancel at once at 0.
- CS-PROC-11 hazard: `StreamWriter(pipe, Encoding.UTF8)` emits EF BB BF on an anonymous pipe, and `StandardInputEncoding=Encoding.UTF8` sends EF BB BF to a child, on both TFMs.
- The BIN pin gate and the triangulate script behave as the file states.

Instruction judgments
- The rule text is sound where it is checkable, but it has no applicability and no exception form for four well-run shapes: a multi-project monorepo, a netstandard2.0 library, a long-lived RPC child, and a protocol-defined digest or lock-file idiom. These are failures 3 to 9, 14 and 16.
- Two further process rules fit real code badly. PROC-17 forbids `CancelKeyPress` and `ProcessExit` handlers, but Bicep.Cli and LangServer are applications that own them. CS-PROC-03's bare-name PATH lookup for `docker-credential-*` is satisfiable through the resolver contract, so I do not count it.

failures.problem: The Conventions missing-operand guard `for d in $SRC; do [ -d "$d" ] || ...` passes silently when SRC is unset or empty. Every cell then runs `rg ... $SRC` with no path operand, so rg searches stdin when stdin is a pipe (CI) or the whole cwd. Empty output reads as pass. The index form `${SRC:?MISSING SRC}` is not what processes.md uses.
failures.evidence: bash -c 'unset SRC; for d in $SRC; do ...; done; echo $?' prints guard exit 0. With `echo | bash -c 'unset SRC; rg -n -g "*.cs" "Environment\s*\.\s*Clear" $SRC'` rg exits 1 with nothing printed. With a pipe carrying text on stdin the same rg scans stdin and not the repo.
failures.fix: Replace the loop with `: "${SRC:?MISSING SRC}"` before the loop, and make every `$SRC` cell run behind that guard, or write the operand as `"${SRC:?MISSING SRC}"` where it is a single path.

failures.problem: processes.md says every row opens with its applicability tag from the index and calls this family `[launches a CLI]`, but the index defines the tag as `[cli-wrapper]` (and the Non-Negotiables use `[cli-wrapper]`). binaries.md has zero tags and the index defines no tag for download or binary acquisition.
failures.evidence: grep -c on processes.md finds 24 `[launches a CLI]` rows. Index Conventions lists `[always] [stj] [cli-wrapper] [packable-library] [mtp] [gha] [greenfield]`. binaries.md has 0 tags, so CS-BIN-11/14/15 cells give 82/80/35 hits on refit, an HTTP library that downloads nothing.
failures.fix: Use the index tag `[cli-wrapper]` in processes.md. Add a download tag to the index (for example `[downloads-binary]`) and put it on every CS-BIN row, or state in the binaries.md header that the family applies only to a library that locates or downloads a binary.

failures.problem: CS-PROC-02 requires exactly one launch seam per repository, and P9 stops at that count and checks no seam member. Bicep ships five launch sites in five projects that wrap four different things. The cell and P9 give no way to express one seam per wrapped tool. P9 prints `MISSING one seam file` for five seams, which is the wrong wording for more than one.
failures.evidence: CS-PROC-02#1 prints 5 paths: ClientProcessLauncher.cs, GrpcLocalExtension.cs, BicepClient.cs, BicepInstaller.cs, DockerCredentialProvider.cs. P9 on bicep prints `MISSING one seam file` and never checks UseShellExecute, CreateNoWindow or the redirects of any of the five.
failures.fix: Scope the rule to one seam per wrapped tool (per library or project), run the seam check per project directory (SRC per project), and word P9 as `expected exactly 1 seam file, found N`.

failures.problem: CS-PROC-01 (ArgumentList), CS-PROC-09 (WaitForExitAsync), CS-PROC-14 (Kill(entireProcessTree:true)) and, in binaries.md, CS-BIN-12 and CS-BIN-13 (File.SetUnixFileMode, CreateDirectory with UnixFileMode) require APIs that do not exist on netstandard2.0. Bicep.RpcClient targets netstandard2.0 on purpose. Neither file has a legacy-TFM clause. The only available way to set the exec bit there is the `chmod` shell-out, which CS-BIN-17 forbids with no exception.
failures.evidence: A netstandard2.0 probe fails to compile: CS1061 ArgumentList, CS1501 Kill(true), CS1061 WaitForExitAsync, CS0117 File.SetUnixFileMode, CS0103 UnixFileMode. src/Bicep.RpcClient/Bicep.RpcClient.csproj has `<TargetFramework>netstandard2.0</TargetFramework>` with the comment `intentionally targeting netstandard2.0`. BicepInstaller.cs:121 `FileName = "chmod"` is a CS-BIN-17 and CS-PROC-03 hit.
failures.fix: Add a `[greenfield]`-style tag, or an explicit legacy-TFM clause, to PROC-01/09/14 and BIN-12/13/17 naming the netstandard2.0 fallback (Arguments with a documented quoting helper, root-only Kill plus sync WaitForExit, chmod via a fixed argv) and its limits.

failures.class: No sanctioned form for a legitimate use
failures.problem: CS-PROC-14 says never create a job object. The VS client does it on purpose, with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so the language-server child dies when Visual Studio itself crashes. Tree kill cannot do that; only a job object (or .NET 11 KillOnParentExit, which the file's own header lists as an upgrade re-check) does. The rationale argues only about Kill versus job object for cancellation.
failures.evidence: CS-PROC-14#2 prints 10 lines on bicep: src/vs-bicep/Bicep.VSLanguageServerClient/ProcessTracker/JobObjectProcessTracker.cs:41,61,91 (CreateJobObject, SetInformationJobObject, AssignProcessToJobObject) and NativeMethods.cs. The doc comment reads `Allows processes to be automatically killed if this parent process unexpectedly quits`.
failures.fix: Add a sanctioned form: a job object is allowed for parent-death cleanup on Windows (one class, KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, no use for cancellation), until KillOnParentExit is available.

failures.problem: The launch-seam greps look only for ProcessStartInfo, Process.Start and new Process. ClientProcessLauncher.CreateProcessForArm64 launches through a Win32 CreateProcess P/Invoke with a string command line (needed to request a native arm64 launch of an AnyCPU exe). That is a second launch path with string argv and no environment scrub, and no cell sees it. The rule also names no form for such a launcher.
failures.evidence: src/vs-bicep/Bicep.VSLanguageServerClient/ProcessLauncher/ClientProcessLauncher.cs:103 NativeMethods.CreateProcess(...) with `string cmdLine = $"\"{exePath}\" {args}"`. The same file appears in CS-PROC-02#1 only through its Amd64 branch.
failures.fix: Extend the seam grep and P9 with `\bCreateProcess(W|A)?\s*\(` and `DllImport[^;]*CreateProcess`, and add a sanctioned form for a native-arm64 launch that states its quoting and environment duties.

failures.problem: The second CS-PROC-11 grep needs `Standard...` to appear after `new StreamWriter(`. The common property-assignment form puts it before: `StandardInput = new StreamWriter(pipe, Encoding.UTF8, ...)`. That form sends a UTF-8 BOM to the child stdin and is not matched. P3 flags the file only for the other launch path.
failures.evidence: ClientProcessLauncher.cs:183 `StandardInput = new StreamWriter(new FileStream(stdInHandle, FileAccess.Write, 4096, false), Encoding.UTF8, 4096, leaveOpen: true);` prints nothing from the cell. A net8.0 and net10.0 probe shows `StreamWriter(pipe, Encoding.UTF8)` and `StandardInputEncoding = Encoding.UTF8` both deliver EF BB BF 61.
failures.fix: Change the pattern to `Standard\w+\s*=\s*new\s+StreamWriter\s*\([^;]*Encoding\.UTF8\b` as an extra alternative, plus the existing one.

failures.problem: P13 and the CS-PROC-12 check match only the literal `StandardInput.Write*`. DockerCredentialProvider writes the secret-bearing stdin through an alias (`using (var writer = process.StandardInput) { await writer.WriteAsync(registry) ... }`) with no StandardInputEncoding. P13 prints nothing.
failures.evidence: DockerCredentialProvider.cs:57-62 uses `writer.WriteAsync` on `process.StandardInput`. P13 output for bicep is empty. P3 does print that file, but for the missing encoding, not because of the write.
failures.fix: Match `=\s*[\w.]*StandardInput\b` aliases in P13 (any file that obtains `.StandardInput` and has no `StandardInputEncoding`).

failures.class: No sanctioned form for a legitimate use
failures.problem: CS-PROC-09 bans ReadToEndAsync, Begin*ReadLine and OutputDataReceived absolutely and models every child as run-to-completion with captured output. Two well-run shapes break it on purpose. DockerCredentialProvider starts both ReadToEndAsync tasks before it writes stdin, which is deadlock-safe, for a small output from a user-installed trusted helper. GrpcLocalExtension forwards a long-lived gRPC extension host's stdout and stderr to the trace log through BeginOutputReadLine and ErrorDataReceived, with no capture and no EOF wait. CS-PROC-17 likewise forbids CancelKeyPress and ProcessExit, but Bicep.Cli and LangServer are applications that own those handlers.
failures.evidence: DockerCredentialProvider.cs:54-55 concurrent ReadToEndAsync before the stdin write at :57. GrpcLocalExtension.cs:78-95 OutputDataReceived/ErrorDataReceived, BeginErrorReadLine, BeginOutputReadLine. Bicep.Cli/Program.cs:178,184 and Bicep.LangServer/Program.cs:120,126 install CancelKeyPress and ProcessExit.
failures.fix: Add sanctioned forms: concurrent ReadToEndAsync of both streams is allowed for a bounded, trusted helper whose stdout is small and cap-checked, and event-mode log forwarding is allowed for a long-lived child whose exit is detected through Exited. Scope PROC-17 to a library and say that an application owns process-wide handlers.

failures.problem: Several cells fire mostly on unrelated code outside their subject. P2 and P10 key on the substring 'token' (JToken, SemanticToken, UnmatchedTokens, TokenType). P2 also uses `-U` with `[^)]*`, so it spans members. The CS-PROC-03 `FileName` cell hits `const string FileName = "main.json"`. P6 hits an unused `using System.Security.AccessControl`. The `"--format"` cell hits the CLI's own option constants. P3 flags a `RedirectStandardOutput` that is never decoded (the chmod call). CancelAfter and GetAsync cells match comments (UniTask) and Azure SDK clients.
failures.evidence: P2: 11 files, 1 true positive (BicepDeploymentStartParams `string token`), 10 false positives. P10: 9 of 9 false positives (bicep 6, refit 3). CS-PROC-03#1: 5 of 6 are `FileName` constants. P6: 1 hit, a using directive. CS-PROC-07#1: Bicep.Cli CliConstants.cs:88 and ArgumentConstants.cs:14. CS-PROC-15#2 on UniTask matches a comment (TimeoutController.cs:8).
failures.fix: Make P2 and P10 case-sensitive on identifier boundaries and exclude type names ending in Token. Require `ProcessStartInfo` in the same statement for FileName. Skip lines starting with `//` and `using` lines.

failures.problem: binaries.md excludes tests with `{[Tt]est,*.[Tt]est,*[Tt]ests}`. The index and processes.md use `*[Tt]est*`. The narrow form lets test-helper libraries through, which is the multiplication the file's own Defaults bullet says it avoids. The wide form excluded no product directory on any of the five trees.
failures.evidence: File counts differ: bicep 1247 (processes glob) vs 1302 (binaries glob), refit 669 vs 732. The leaked files are src/Bicep.Testing (about 37), Bicep.RegistryModuleTool.TestFixtures, vs-bicep/...TestServices, src/Refit.Testing and examples under *Testing* directories. find found only test-named product directories nowhere.
failures.fix: Use `-g '!**/*[Tt]est*/**'` in every BIN cell, as the index Conventions do.

failures.problem: Hard-coded operands that exit 2 or fail on every tree. The cells scan the literal `src` and `src/Bootstrap` instead of the SRC variable the shared decision introduced. The README cell reads only root README.md, while the packed README of the real package is src/Bicep.RpcClient/PACKAGE.md. The pin gate hard-codes `ocx-pins.json` (jq exits 2). The canary block hard-codes `canary/canary.csproj`, and on a tree with no canary prints `bad net8.0 exit 1`, which equals the expected value.
failures.evidence: CS-BIN-12#1 and CS-BIN-13#1 exit 2 on all 5 trees (src/Bootstrap missing). Retargeted to src they print 10 and 7 noise lines on bicep (app file writes). jq on ocx-pins.json exits 2. BIN-26 cell prints nothing for Bicep.RpcClient, whose trust text, if any, lives in PACKAGE.md (src/Bicep.RpcClient/PACKAGE.md has no verify or trust text).
failures.fix: Use `"${SRC:?MISSING SRC}"` and an `INSTALL_DIR` operand, scan `**/README.md` and the project's PackageReadmeFile, take the pin file path as an operand, and make the canary block fail with a named message when its project is missing.

failures.problem: The CS-BIN-07 cell keys on `Convert.ToHexString` only. Bicep builds its hex with `BitConverter.ToString(h).Replace("-","").ToLowerInvariant()` and compares with `string.Equals(..., StringComparison.Ordinal)` and a `DigestComparer` (StringComparer.Ordinal). That is the defect the rule forbids, and the cell prints nothing.
failures.evidence: AzureContainerRegistryManager.cs:336-339 and :347 `string.Equals(descriptor.Digest, digestFromContents, StringComparison.Ordinal)`. OciDescriptor.cs:49 `BitConverter.ToString(hashValue).Replace("-", "")`. CS-BIN-07#1 is empty on bicep.
failures.fix: Add `BitConverter\.ToString` and `ToLower(Invariant)?\s*\(\)\s*(==|!=)` and `Equals\([^;]*[Dd]igest` as patterns, or make the rule check the compare site instead of the hex producer.

failures.class: No sanctioned form for a legitimate use
failures.problem: CS-BIN-07 says never compare hex strings and always compare bytes through the CS-SEC-08 helper. For an OCI digest, the registry protocol defines a lowercase `sha256:<hex>` string that is public and not a secret, and Bicep compares the descriptor string with the recomputed string. An exact ordinal string compare is correct there and has no timing exposure. The rule offers no form for a protocol-defined digest string.
failures.evidence: Bicep.Core/Registry/AzureContainerRegistryManager.cs:335-340 and ValidateManifestResponse :344-352 compare the OCI digest strings after a size check. OciArtifactReferenceFacts.cs:44 validates `^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$`.
failures.fix: Add a sanctioned form: a protocol-defined lowercase hex digest compared ordinally against the descriptor is allowed when both sides are public and produced by the same lowercase formatter; keep the byte compare for secrets and pins.

failures.problem: Every BIN cell is a negative grep, so a download path with no verification at all passes. Bicep.RpcClient downloads an executable, applies no hash or signature check and defaults to the latest release. The CS-BIN-06 patterns (`?? "latest"`, `version = "latest"`) do not see that default, which is implemented as a null version plus a `/releases/latest` fetch.
failures.evidence: BicepInstaller.cs:56-62 downloads to a temp file then chmod and move, with no SHA anywhere in src/Bicep.RpcClient (rg for sha256|checksum|hash|verify finds none). BicepClientFactory.cs:53 calls GetLatestBicepVersion when BicepVersion is null; BicepClientConfiguration.cs:34 `Defaults to the latest available version`. CS-BIN-06#1, BIN-07#1, BIN-22#1 and BIN-25#1 are all empty.
failures.fix: Add a positive cell for BIN-07 and BIN-20: a file that calls HttpClient and writes a file must also call SHA256 and the CS-SEC-08 helper. Add `releases/latest|GetLatest\w*Version` to the BIN-06 cell.

failures.class: No sanctioned form for a legitimate use
failures.problem: CS-BIN-12 prescribes CreateNew plus Move(overwrite:false) plus a sidecar and bans FileMode.OpenOrCreate and FileMode.Create. The installer's cross-process lock-file idiom (OpenOrCreate, FileShare.None) is a legitimate way to serialize an install and is flagged. The temp-then-publish step uses File.Create and File.Replace, which are not in the cell's list, so the actual write is missed.
failures.evidence: CS-BIN-12#1 retargeted prints BicepInstaller.cs:190,193 (`FileMode.OpenOrCreate`, FileShare.None) and Bicep.IO/FileSystem/FileSystemStreamLock.cs:27,30 (same idiom). BicepInstaller.cs:57 `File.Create(tempFilePath)` and :217 `File.Replace` do not print.
failures.fix: Name a lock-file form (OpenOrCreate with FileShare.None on a dedicated `.lock` path only, never on the binary), and add File.Create, File.OpenWrite and File.Replace to the cell.

failures.problem: The CS-BIN-14 cell matches `new HttpClient(` and `HttpClient x = new(` but not an object-initializer construction without parentheses. The 80 refit hits are out of scope, but they show the cell finds neither of refit's two `new HttpClient { ... }` sites.
failures.evidence: src/examples/SampleUsingLocalApi/ConsoleApplication/Program.cs:41 `new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new("http://localhost:61868") }` and src/examples/BlazorWasmIssue2065/Program.cs:16 `new HttpClient { BaseAddress = ... }`. An independent rg for `new\s+HttpClient\b(?!\s*\()` finds both.
failures.fix: Add `new\s+HttpClient\s*(\{|$)` to the cell's pattern list.

failures.problem: The BIN-08, BIN-11 and BIN-14 cells scan every file of src, not only the manifest and archive path. In a real multi-purpose codebase they mostly hit unrelated code: 25 of 28 BIN-08 hits are compiler or linter regexes, 6 of 8 BIN-11#2 hits are Azure SDK `.GetAsync`, and BIN-14 asks for exactly one HttpClient while Bicep.Core legitimately registers a typed client and McpServer builds its own.
failures.evidence: BIN-08 on bicep prints Lexer-adjacent regexes such as Linter/Common/LinterResourceTypePatterns.cs:11 and TypeSystem/Providers/Az/AzResourceTypeProvider.cs:26-27. BIN-11#2 on bicep prints DeploymentProcessor.cs:219 `stacksClient.GetAsync(deploymentName, ...)` and ArmDeploymentProvider.cs:71. BIN-14 prints OrasOciRegistryTransport.cs:40,209 `CreateClient()` methods.
failures.fix: Scope each cell to the installer directory operand and the manifest file only, and require an HttpClient receiver for the GetAsync and SendAsync patterns.

failures.problem: No cell detects a missing kill, timeout or cancellation classification outside `src/Process`, and the ban cells are negative only. DockerCredentialProvider waits with `WaitForExitAsync(cancellationToken)` and never kills the helper on cancel or timeout. BicepClient.TryKillProcess is a bare `Kill()` followed by a synchronous `WaitForExit(10000)`. Both are caught, if at all, by RS0030 alone.
failures.evidence: DockerCredentialProvider.cs:64 `await process.WaitForExitAsync(cancellationToken)` with no Kill in the file. BicepClient.cs:200-215. P11 and P14 run only on `src/Process` (exit 2 on all five trees, so unverified).
failures.fix: Add a positive cell for CS-PROC-14/15: a file that creates a Process must also contain `Kill(entireProcessTree` and a timeout source, and run P11 and P14 over the seam file found by CS-PROC-02 instead of `src/Process`.

failures.fix: State: exit 1 is a CS-BUILD-21 finding; the owner adds sdk.version (the SDK the repo builds with) in the release commit; run the remaining steps only on that SDK and put the SDK in the receipt.

failures.problem: The pack path assumes MinVer from tags and a provider variable for ContinuousIntegrationBuild. A repo with `Version` from `-p:Version=` and CIB/snupkg keyed on `$(CI)` packs 1.0.0 with no snupkg using the literal step 4 command. The skill has no sanctioned form: step 3 only mentions another provider's variable, and the step 4 command has no version argument. CS-PKG-07 `fetch-depth: 0` is also a false positive when the version comes from `git describe --exact-match`.
failures.evidence: NSubstitute: literal step 4 -> `pack exit 0`, artifacts/NSubstitute.1.0.0.nupkg, `ls artifacts/*.snupkg` fails, `version ok` not printed. With `CI=true -p:Version=6.3.0`: 6.3.0 nupkg + snupkg, validate exit 0, reproducible.
failures.fix: Step 3/4: say which variables to export are read from the props (`CI`, `TF_BUILD`, ...), allow `-p:Version=${TAG#v}` when the repo has no MinVer, and mark that as a CS-PKG-06 finding rather than a stop.

failures.file: rules/dotnet-build/packaging.md (block workflow-pins, run by SKILL step 8)
failures.class: No sanctioned form for a legitimate use
failures.problem: The first CS-PKG-11 grep flags `user: ${{ secrets.NUGET_USER }}`, the profile-name form NuGet's Trusted Publishing docs use. The pattern `secrets\.[A-Za-z_]*NUGET[A-Za-z_]*` matches every NUGET-named secret, not an API key.
failures.evidence: release_packages.yml:40 `user: ${{ secrets.NUGET_USER }}` printed by the first grep; the same workflow uses NuGet/login (no API-key secret).
failures.fix: Restrict the pattern to key-like secrets (`NUGET_API_KEY|NUGET_KEY|APIKEY`) or exclude lines under `user:`.

failures.problem: The CS-PKG-09/11/12/13 blocks need CIF and REL (`${CIF:?MISSING CIF}`), but step 8 never defines them. Run as written, the first block aborts. The skill only says the blocks name release.yml.
failures.evidence: `bash -c 'unset CIF REL; grep ... ${CIF:?MISSING CIF}'` -> 'CIF: MISSING CIF'. With CIF=.github/workflows REL=.github/workflows/release_packages.yml they ran.
failures.fix: Add a line to step 8: `CIF=.github/workflows REL=<the publish workflow the per-file loop prints>`.

failures.problem: The CS-SEC-10 leak line lists every PackageReference lacking PrivateAssets=all, so any library with a legitimate runtime dependency prints findings; only System.Text.Json is subtracted and there is no owner-exception route. With no Directory.Packages*.props the `rg ... $PROPS` operand is empty, so rg reads stdin or the cwd. The MISSING-OPERAND note is in the rule, not in the skill.
failures.evidence: NSubstitute: output `Castle.Core`, `System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions` (runtime deps), plus `MISSING-OPERAND Directory.Packages.props`. rg with empty PROPS needed `< /dev/null` to return.
failures.fix: Subtract the nuspec's declared dependency ids from the leak list, or add a written owner-exception route as CS-SEC-09 has. Guard the rg line on non-empty PROPS.

failures.problem: `test exit` must be 0, but a multi-TFM test project whose legs need runtimes the host lacks exits 1. The skill gives no route (`-f`) or diagnosis for exit 150 / a missing `mono`.
failures.evidence: NSubstitute tests target net462;net8.0;net9.0;net10.0. `dotnet test --solution ...` exit 1: 'Exit code: 150 ... Microsoft.NETCore.App 9.0.0 not found' and 'RunCommand mono ... No such file'. `-f net10.0` -> exit 0, 900 tests.
failures.fix: Add: exit 1 with 'Zero tests ran' + exit 150 or a missing RunCommand is a host runtime gap; install the runtime or run `-f <installed TFM>` and say so in the receipt.

failures.class: Organic failure outside a plant-built catalogue
failures.problem: `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin` fixes a shallow clone but not a blob-less one. Nerdbank.GitVersioning's managed git reader does not lazy-fetch, so the build fails with MSB4018 and no skill row maps it. Step 1 mentions blob-less only for tags.
failures.evidence: Bicep (blob:none): `build exit 1`, 1330 x 'error MSB4018 ... Unable to get version from commit ... blob object a91b4e0d... could not be found'. After `git rev-list --objects HEAD -- version.json | awk 'NF>1{print $1}' | git cat-file --batch`, `build exit 0`.
failures.fix: Step 3: on a partial clone (`git config remote.origin.promisor`) prefetch the version file blobs or `git fetch --refetch --no-filter`, and name the MSB4018 symptom.

failures.class: Unbounded side effect of a prescribed command
failures.problem: `NUGET_PACKAGES=$(mktemp -d)`, the step 7 `R=$(mktemp -d)` clone and the step 11 smoke dir are never removed. A trap cleanup after the restore would break the next lines, because `build --no-restore` reads that path from obj/project.assets.json.
failures.evidence: nsub full slnx cold restore left 669 MB; Bicep 2.9 GB per run; step 11 smoke dirs 117 and 131 MB. A repeat of the nsub restore block made another 669 MB.
failures.fix: State the size and delete the packages folder after step 6 (export NUGET_PACKAGES once, `rm -rf` at the end of step 8), and add `rm -rf "$R" "$d"` after the checks.

failures.class: Organic failure outside a plant-built catalogue
failures.problem: On an AOT publish with `-v:q` the linker cause is dropped. A host without zlib dev prints only `collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status` / MSB3073. The prerequisites list (clang, zlib1g-dev) is Ubuntu-only and does not tie the symptom to the cause. gcc worked once -lz resolved.
failures.evidence: Refit.NativeAotSmoke: `publish exit 1`, IL count 0, pub.log shows only the collect2 line. At -v:m: `/usr/sbin/ld.bfd: cannot find -lz`. With a libz.so stub on LIBRARY_PATH (not in the skill): exit 0, 5.0 MB, run exit 0.
failures.fix: Step 10: for an AOT publish exit 1 with 'ld returned 1', rerun that one command at -v:m; `cannot find -lz` or `clang not found` means a missing prerequisite. List the zlib dev package for each distro.

failures.problem: The 'count equals files shipped' heuristic cannot tell foreign-RID content assets (Windows DLLs from a Cosmos package) from needed sidecars. Bicep sets IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract and `out/bicep` alone runs, yet the count is 6, so the release-ships comparison is either 6 (directory) or a false 'sidecar needed' (exe only).
failures.evidence: `find out -maxdepth 1 -type f ! -name '*.pdb' ...` -> 6 (bicep + Cosmos.CRTCompat.dll, msvcp140.dll, vcruntime140*.dll, Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos.ServiceInterop.dll). Copy of `out/bicep` alone: `run exit 0`.
failures.fix: Say the check compares only the files the release ships, and that a RID-foreign file that the exe-alone run does not need is not a finding.

failures.problem: `ls artifacts/Acme.Lib.0.0.0* 2>/dev/null` is meant to print nothing when it passes. In zsh (the shell this host and the agent use) the no-match case prints `zsh: no matches found` regardless of 2>/dev/null, which reads as a failure.
failures.evidence: zsh -c 'ls artifacts/NSubstitute.0.0.0* 2>/dev/null' -> 'zsh:1: no matches found', rc 1; the same line under sh -> nothing, rc 2.
failures.fix: Use `find artifacts -name 'Acme.Lib.0.0.0*'`, or state that the blocks run under bash/sh.

failures.problem: A library takes its bump from the CS-API-14 PublicAPI signals, but a repo without PublicAPI files has no mechanical signal and the skill gives no fallback. I chose v6.3.0 myself.
failures.evidence: NSubstitute: `git ls-files '*PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt' | wc -l` -> 0 (CS-API-11 finding), no *REMOVED* or suppression data to read.
failures.fix: Add a fallback: with no PublicAPI files the bump is the owner's call and the missing files are the CS-API-11 finding. Ask the owner before step 3.

new_classes.name: Prescribed cleanup breaks a later prescribed command
new_classes.mechanism: A block cleans up correctly (Gate trap rm -rf "$NUGET_PACKAGES", DN-RULE-05 rm -rf $p), but the command it ran left tree state pointing at what it removed: obj/project.assets.json names the deleted packages folder. Every later --no-restore/--no-build command, the agent's next build or the IDE fails with NETSDK1064 or misreports ('No test projects were found'). Each block passes alone; the failure exists only in sequence, and round 1's du-before/after check cannot see it (its prescribed trap fix causes it). Classifier reproduced on GuardClauses: restore --packages $p, rm -rf $p, build --no-restore -> exit 1 NETSDK1064.
new_classes.check: Run the documented blocks in stated order on one tree, then a plain `dotnet build "$SLN" --no-restore` and `dotnet test --no-build`; each must behave as after a normal restore. Any block that redirects or deletes state another command reads (packages folder, obj/, global.json, git config) must restore it before returning (e.g. a final plain `dotnet restore "$SLN"`) or work in a disposable `git worktree add` copy.
